Find taxa whose values for a trait are all the same within a dataset

Source: R/dataset_checks.R
dataset_check_duplicates_within_dataset.Rd

Lists the taxa that have several values for a trait in a dataset, all of them identical. This is usually a value recorded once for the species, such as its growth form, repeated on every row of individual measurements, or a single bulked measurement reported for each individual that contributed to it. Neither is disallowed, so dataset_test() does not check for it, but a value repeated this way counts as several observations when it is one, and is usually better entered once, with the entity_type it describes.

dataset_check_duplicates_within_dataset(
  database,
  dataset_ids = NULL,
  trait_types = "categorical"
)

Arguments

database

Compiled database object, e.g. austraits

dataset_ids

dataset_id's to check. The default, NULL, checks every dataset in the database.

trait_types

Types of trait to check. The default checks categorical traits only: numeric values repeat by coincidence, especially for traits reported to few significant figures, but c("categorical", "numeric") checks both.

Value

A list of two tibbles:

summary

One row per dataset and trait with at least one taxon whose values are all identical. n_taxa_several is the number of taxa with more than one value for the trait, and n_taxa_repeated the number of those whose values are all identical, counting a taxon once for each name, location and value type. entity_type lists the entity types of the trait's values. Sorted by dataset, then with the traits repeated for the largest share of taxa first.

taxa

One row per taxon, name, location and value type whose values are all identical, with the value and how many records hold it (n_records).

Details

Values are compared within a taxon as the source names it, by original_name, at a single location. Values for names the source gives separately but the taxonomy merges into one taxon_name, as for synonyms in a flora, are separate records of the source rather than repeats; and a taxon scored once at each of several sites, as in a survey of fire responses, has one value per population, as it should. Neither is counted. Values of different value_types are not compared either, so a minimum and a maximum that happen to agree are not a repeat. What remains is the same value given more than once for one name at one place: copied down to individuals, or repeated across method_contexts, temporal_contexts or sources, any of which may be intended.

A trait repeated for nearly every taxon with several values, so that n_taxa_repeated is close to n_taxa_several in summary, has most likely been copied down a column, or mapped from two columns that agree. A few repeated taxa among many that vary is what a trait that varies little looks like.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dataset_check_duplicates_within_dataset(austraits, "Tsakalos_2020")
} # }
